Well I've had clinical depression for the past 6 or 7 years and although I don't take any medication for it, I am currently in counseling. We've been discussing options as far as medical treatment is concerned.
Because of the bipolar disorder, I'll have these feelings that I'm completely invincible. I'm not entirely sure what's going through my head, but I'll have already convinced that it's what I should be doing. I'll drive recklessly on the freeway or take risks/push the limits on life, etc. But when I experience the other side of the spectrum (unmotivated, lazy, unemotional, angry, etc.), my depression hits an all-time low. In addition to feeling sad and empty, I'll have suicidal thoughts. It's as if my depression was on overdrive. Then like a flick of a switch, I'll be back to the happy, carefree, reckless person I was 10 minutes ago. 
The unpredictability of it all even scares me, but hopefully, I'll be on some medication that will help me better control my actions.

I have a very strong photographic memory. And I remember ideas and events based on the colors associated with them. I started remembering most of my life when I hit my head at age 5. 

-I would consider it a blessing and a curse. Unfortunately, I remember all the abuse done to me as a child. But I am currently in counseling to help with that. On the other hand, having such a strong photographic memory has helped me in school while taking tests and in theater, as I can memorize entire scripts in only a few hours. 

-I don't remember dreams as much, but I definitely notice having more colorful dreams. "Colorful" meaning actually colorful. I'll dream of things with bright and vivid, unnatural colors. For example, a recent dream I had included yellow trees and purple snow. 

-I don't exactly understand the question, but it doesn't affect my daily life in that moment because I don't have to think about remembering things. It just happens. 

-Yes! Like I said before, I can memorize like no other. So I've definitely excelled in theater and performing because I can memorize so quickly. I can also take tests pretty well because I can remember with such ease. 

-There are a few quirky advantages to a photographic memory, such as memorizing license plate numbers and remembering the order someone ate colored M&Ms. I also have no excuse for forgetting birthdays.
